title: Improve heavily masked and broadband foreground detection
description: The current learner detects only 14.2% of events and correctly recognises 0.6% of repeats at -6 dB. Investigate adaptive thresholds/background estimation and temporal features without retaining extra noise. Explicitly evaluate broadband and sustained events currently rejected by duration/flatness heuristics; retain frozen historical baselines and held-out settings.
acceptance_criteria: Report paired true-event recall and nuisance admissions with uncertainty; demonstrate improvement over archived masked baseline without hiding missed detections or retuning on final evaluation recordings.

title: Build a background-aware acoustic scene and novelty-learning experiment
description: Implement seeded coloured room noise, hum/drift, foreground events, nuisance transients, reverberation and microphone filtering; learn recurring foreground novelty without oracle labels; compare against whole-clip MFCC memory using identical audio and report false admissions, event recall, habituation and reproducible per-seed outputs. Add meaningful regression checks and document limits.
close_reason: Implemented continuous seeded acoustic scenes, mixture-only foreground novelty memory, recurrence ablation and historical MFCC comparator, CLI, docs and archived evidence. Eight tests pass, original grader scores 1.0, installed CLI works, compilation and diff checks pass. Audited 7200 raw decisions against reported per-seed figures/source hashes. Masked/recorded/broadband limitations explicitly preserved and filed for follow-up.

title: Integrate selective listening with capture and mood without mixing feature schemas
description: ForegroundLearner is currently a separate perception experiment. Add an opt-in capture/controller path so candidate, learned and recognised outcomes drive appropriate displays and avoid automatic background replay. Keep its 96-D temporal context separate from legacy 13-D MFCC voice exemplars; define persistence and restart behaviour before combining either memory with dream/repertoire operations.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise a capture replay through controller transitions, including calibration and silence; prevent incompatible feature comparisons; verify no background-triggered vocal response; preserve legacy demo and grader behaviour.

title: Compare recurrence with learning-progress and one-off importance policies
description: Separate learnable novelty from stochastic unpredictability and human relevance. Compare current two-sighting confirmation with uncertainty or learning-progress admission, habituation to repeating nuisances, and a bounded short-term response to important one-off events. Use equal memory budgets and an explicit experimental definition or supplied feedback for importance rather than assuming tonality equals value.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate recurring useful events, recurring nuisance, random distractors and one-off foregrounds; report immediate responses separately from permanent memory, repeat recognition and false admissions. Document any supervised feedback and keep it out of mixture-only baselines.

title: Build a held-out recorded foreground and background benchmark
description: Add owned or appropriately licensed recordings with provenance and disjoint source recordings for development versus evaluation. Include speech, footsteps, long alarms and overlapping sources, varied backgrounds, independent room/microphone conditions and calibrated SNR mixtures. Maintain waveform-only learner access, reproducible manifests and raw per-window outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Document licenses and splits; include at least tonal, broadband and long-duration foreground cases; provide paired baseline runs with per-seed recall, wrong recognition and nuisance admissions at 0 dB and below.

title: Evaluate recorded and heavily masked foreground sounds beyond tonal novelty
description: Follow up ch-e73: new foreground learner recognises repeats at 0/+6/+12 dB but fails at -6 dB (14.2% detection, 0.6% correct repeat recognition over stress seeds 200-204). Build licensed/owned recorded foreground-background mixtures including speech, footsteps, long alarms and overlapping sources; vary rooms and microphones independently; compare recurrence admission with learning-progress or importance signals so broadband and important one-off events are not filtered out. Preserve waveform-only learner access, per-seed false-admission and true-event-recall metrics, raw traces, and held-out recordings. Evidence: papers/01-foreground-novelty.md and papers/results/foreground-novelty.
acceptance_criteria: Child tasks provide a held-out recorded-audio benchmark, improved masked/broadband detection, an evaluated importance/admission policy, and a schema-safe capture/mood integration. Preserve the existing main/stress evidence and report both true-event recall and nuisance admission rates.

title: Make dream sampling reproducible and reconcile reachable mood states

Inject controlled randomness, explicitly decide intended state reachability, and verify supported transition coverage. See revised pilot paper sections 5.8 and 9.7-9.9; no implementation changes were made during manuscript review.

See papers/00-pilot-study.md sections 4 and 9.1.

Historical replication and mood/RNG follow-ups recorded as ch-juc and ch-42z.

title: Write academic-style pilot study paper (papers/00-pilot-study.md)
description: Full write-up: background/related work (13 cited sources with verified authors: Leitao & Gahr 2024, Goldstein/King/West 2003, Kuhl 2003, Boncoraglio & Saino 2007, Friston 2010, Zhang et al. 2024, Lou et al. 2026, Zhu et al. 2025, Zaslavsky et al. 2018, Rita et al. 2022, Lewis 1969, Skyrms 2010, Davis & Mermelstein 1980, plus DreamCoder/Ellis et al. 2021 and clebran-arc-agi), system architecture, all 8 sim/ experiments (ch-50/52/53/54/63/33 results plus the run_demo guardrail proof and the call-DSL fitness-metric finding), the clebran-arc-agi structural comparison, limitations, and a 7-item next-steps agenda. Numbers cross-checked against shared/research_backlog.md's final recorded figures before writing.

title: Test replacing Repertoire's index-based default tie-break with a random one
description: ch-63 ruled out the relevance gate as the cause of coarse (2-of-6) grounding in grounding_demo.py, via a clean 4-threshold x 10-seed sweep with zero effect even at threshold=0.9. The real suspect is Repertoire._base_default(call_index) = 0.5 - 0.001*call_index: a fixed index-order ramp means call#0 wins any brand-new context by default whenever no call has a qualifying exemplar yet, regardless of relevance-gate strictness. Test: replace the index ramp with a per-instance random tie-break fixed at construction (deterministic across repeated closest_call() calls, just not correlated with index) and re-run grounding_demo.py's 10-seed sweep - does distinct-pairs count rise above ~2/6 once the structural index bias is removed?

title: Tighten Repertoire's relevance gate to test finer-grained grounding
description: Hypothesis REFUTED, cleanly. Moved RELEVANCE_SIM_THRESHOLD/SAME_CONTEXT_DISTANCE into config.py (were hardcoded in comms.py, violating the project's own convention) and exposed as optional Repertoire constructor overrides (backward compatible, eval grader still scores 1.0). Swept 0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 across 10 seeds each via grounding_demo.py --sweep-thresholds: avg distinct pairs stayed ~2.0/6 at EVERY threshold including 0.9 (near-impossible to clear). No effect at all. Real mechanism must be _base_default()'s index-based tie-break, not the relevance gate - even a near-unreachable gate still leaves call#0 winning any new context by default when nothing else has a qualifying exemplar either. Correctly-targeted follow-up: ch-64.

title: Heed clebran's 'transport not discovery' finding for the two-unit comms track
description: clebran-arc-agi's headline, hard-won result: at matched compute, a single learner mining its own solution library (B5) beats every multi-agent gossip arm (B2/B3/B6/B7/B8/B9), across many control conditions - 'communication is a transport mechanism, not a discovery mechanism' in that domain. Caution for ch-23a/ch-23b: don't expect two-unit comms to make either Chuff learn calls faster/better than a single well-tuned Chuff would alone. The two-unit track's actual value is probably the convention-formation/signaling phenomenon itself (does a stable shared mapping emerge at all - Theme 3.3's grounding question), not a learning-speed win - which is consistent with what two_unit_demo.py already showed (contingent ack produces a stable convention, not obviously a *better* one). Decision: keep the two-unit track framed as a signaling/convention-formation question, not a skill-transfer question, when writing it up.

title: Stitch-style library mining over evolved CallPrograms
description: The B5 central-library result (clebran-arc-agi) says a single learner mining its own solutions into a reusable abstraction library beats multi-agent sharing at matched compute. Port the idea: after evolving CallPrograms toward several different targets (ch-60), mine recurring op-sequences across the best-of-run programs into reusable 'motifs' (clebran's dsl/abstraction.py antiunification algorithm is the reference design). Blocked in practice, not formally: ch-60 found the MFCC-cosine fitness metric accepts structural shortcuts (chirp-as-tone, tone-with-AM-as-chirp) that would bias what gets mined toward 'things that fool cosine similarity' rather than meaningful acoustic building blocks - needs a stricter or multi-target fitness before mining is worth running.

title: Compositional call-construction DSL + evolutionary search (call_dsl.py)
description: Inspired by clebran-arc-agi's linear-IR genome (mutation/crossover/fragment vocabulary) applied to Chuff's much simpler acoustic domain: a CallProgram is one generator op (tone/chirp) plus 0-3 modifier ops (am, envelope), with mutate_const/swap/grow/delete and crossover. dsl_evolution_demo.py (chuff-sim-dsl) evolves a population toward a target sound's MFCC via cosine-similarity fitness. Both a tone target and a wide-chirp target reach ~0.97-0.98 fitness, but via structural shortcuts (a near-zero-width chirp for the tone target; an AM-heavy tone for the chirp target), not the 'intended' generator - see shared/research_backlog.md for the full writeup and why that matters for ch-61.

title: Compare A's and B's independently-converged call-to-sound mappings
description: grounding_demo.py (chuff-sim-grounding): Unit B upgraded to a full second ChuffAgent, both units hear+speak+ack symmetrically. A 10-seed sweep (seeds 0-9, 150 rounds each) - the first 3 runs looked like a fixed acoustic split and that write-up was wrong, corrected after sweeping more seeds - shows: always exactly 2 distinct (A-call,B-call) pairs, always 100% purity per label every seed, and the majority pair is ALWAYS call #0/#0 (Repertoire's untrained index-0 tie-break has a real structural edge). But WHICH 1-2 labels break away from that majority varies by seed (kettle_whistle+bird_call in 3/10, car_horn+dog_bark in 4/10, phone_ring alone in 3/10) with no consistent acoustic theme. Reading: coarse-but-real discrimination driven by presentation-order lock-in (whichever label first falls outside call#0's relevance-gate radius claims a different call and keeps it), not a fixed acoustic category boundary. See shared/research_backlog.md Theme 3.3. Follow-up (tighter relevance gate / remove index bias) tracked as ch-63.

title: Babbling warm-up phase in sim/run_demo.py
description: ChuffAgent.babble() (sim/agent.py): self-reinforces each repertoire call against its own clean signature before any real sound arrives - a naive 'play it once' phase does nothing observable since respond() already lazily caches self-reference on first use, so the mechanism had to be self-directed reinforcement, not just exposure. babbling_experiment.py (chuff-sim-babble), 40 seeds x 6 sounds: babbling changes the first real-world response 73% of the time, landing ~735-770Hz closer to the target's characteristic frequency on average (1007Hz error cold-start vs 271Hz babbled). Clean positive result, held up across seed counts. See shared/research_backlog.md Theme 1.1.

Exposed and fixed two real bugs: a one-pole filter was too gentle, and Repertoire.frequencies used to be sorted, biasing the untrained tie-break. See shared/research_backlog.md Theme 1.2.

title: JSONL call-context/acknowledgement logging
description: All three sim demos (run_demo.py, two_unit_demo.py, grounding_demo.py) were reimplementing JSONL logging ad hoc instead of using the already-implemented comms.log_event() - refactored all three to use it. Doing so surfaced a real latent bug that had existed since two_unit_demo.py was first written: _detect_tone() returns numpy.bool_ (via comparisons on numpy FFT-array scalars), which json.dumps rejects - '--log' had never actually been exercised in testing before, so the crash was never caught. Fixed by explicitly casting to Python float/bool in _detect_tone(). Verified: all three demos now log every round correctly (line count matches round count) and the crash is gone.
